summary: Milestone 12 (Reader Construction Framework) end-to-end acceptance PASSED against the public URL (https://dev-converse.preview.emergentagent.com). Backend: 7/7 pytest passes in /app/backend/tests/test_milestone12_reader_construction.py (5/7 first-run + 2/7 on rerun where the first failure was a test-side theory_history shape bug now fixed, and the second was a transient empty-done SSE frame that the retry pattern now handles). Total wall time ~11m45s across 8 live Claude SSE calls + 2 CRUD smokes, no code changes needed to the app. Frontend: 9/9 UI checks passed against the public URL — ?dev auto-loads writing-area, ambiguous draft (from review request: 'Social media makes people feel connected, which is the problem.') submitted via continue-button produces ai-invitation (~55s SSE), open-dev-panel-button opens Dev Panel, reader-construction-block renders with reader_understanding + likely_reader_questions + assumed_knowledge + clarification_needed + elaboration_needed + precision_risk + next_reader_need ALL populated, scaffolding-control-block still renders with primary_target/mode/cycle_status populated, communicative-purpose-block still renders (cp.primary='persuade'), and new-test-session-button resets to empty writing-area with no ai-invitation. Coverage of the eight requested criteria: (a) reader_construction.applies=true + reader_understanding non-empty verified on every draft turn across all 5 SSE tests (hidden-assumption / ambiguous / inferential-gap / evolving turn1 / evolving turn2 / supported body paragraph); (b) MISUNDERSTANDINGS FLAGGED — hidden-assumption Gatsby draft populated assumed_knowledge ('Reader assumed to already know the symbolic reading — obviously flags an unsupported assumption'), ambiguous draft populated precision_risk ('Reader might take the problem as a rhetorical hook rather than a claim about harm'), inferential-gap teens/phones draft populated elaboration_needed AND clarification_needed; (c) READER-UNDERSTANDING FRAMING — invitations for the ambiguous draft had ZERO grammar-correctness phrases (no grammar/punctuation/spelling/comma-splice/subject-verb-agreement/tense) — precision was taught as shared reader understanding; elaboration invitation for the inferential-gap draft had ZERO word-count/length phrases (no 'add more words'/'make it longer'/'write more'/'increase the length'); (d) M11 STILL SELECTS ONE TARGET — every one of the 6 draft turns had scaffolding_control.primary_target non-empty + instructional_mode in the valid set + cycle_status in {continue, consolidate_and_return, stop}; the ambiguous case shown live: primary_target='Articulating a controlling claim the reader can identify...', mode='developmental_question', cycle_status='continue'; (e) READER MODEL EVOLVES — the photosynthesis two-turn (writing 'Photosynthesis is how plants make food' -> revise adding chloroplasts/water/CO2/sugar/oxygen) produced ru1='Reader knows only that photosynthesis is how plants make food — one bare fact.' and ru2='Reader now knows photosynthesis is how plants make food, that it happens inside...' — the model updated to the newly communicated content; (f) M6-M11 REGRESSION on supported body paragraph — cp.primary='persuade', pf.applies=True, ef.applies=True, cf.applies=True, scaffolding_control populated, reader_construction populated ('The reader understands the claim, sees the example, and grasps that the writer values...'); (g) M1-M5A REGRESSION — theory_history v1..v2 preserved across writing->revise (v1.version=1, v2.version>=2, v1.theory != v_last.theory), currently_relevant_domains 1-3, intervention.focus='writing' + writing_not_content_check non-empty on every non-independence turn, no invented content ('you could add'/'another reason'/'consider adding'/'try adding' — 0 hits across all 6 SSE turns), no stage/level/grade/rubric leaks; (h) FRONTEND — reader-construction-block renders with all fields populated between scaffolding-control-block (M11) and paragraph-function-block (M7), correctly gated by applies=true.

minor.issue: Still returns 200 (not 201) for resource creation. Carry-over from every prior iteration; not blocking.

issues: The Development Panel appears wider than viewport at both 1440x1000 and 1920x1080 — the close-dev-panel-button (top-right X inside the panel header) is positioned outside the visible viewport at both widths and requires horizontal scrolling to reach. The NEW TEST + DEV PANEL buttons in the app header are also partially clipped. This does NOT block M12 acceptance (all reader-construction-block content renders correctly and new-test-session-button works from the main app header), but the dev-only panel would benefit from a max-width or horizontal-scroll container so operators can close it without scrolling. In dev-only usage this is cosmetic.

action_items: None blocking. Milestone 12 acceptance holds end-to-end. All eight requested criteria verified: (a) reader_construction.applies=true + reader_understanding non-empty whenever a draft exists; (b) hidden-assumption -> assumed_knowledge, ambiguous -> precision_risk, inferential-gap -> elaboration_needed OR clarification_needed; (c) precision NOT framed as grammar, elaboration NOT framed as word-count; (d) M11 still selects ONE primary_target on every turn; (e) reader_understanding evolves across turns; (f) M6-M11 preserved (cp.primary + pf/ef/cf.applies + scaffolding_control on a supported body paragraph); (g) M1-M5A intact (theory_history v1..vN preserved with correct {version, telos, theory, created_at} shape, focus='writing', writing_not_content_check populated, no invented content, no stage/level/grade/rubric leaks); (h) reader-construction-block renders in the Dev Panel with all seven M12 fields populated.
Optional (cosmetic): constrain Development Panel width or add horizontal-scroll so the close-panel button is reachable at 1440-1920px viewports.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py (line 199) — ReaderConstruction Pydantic model has exactly the eight fields the review request specifies (applies, reader_understanding, likely_reader_questions, assumed_knowledge, clarification_needed, elaboration_needed, precision_risk, next_reader_need) with the right types (bool + str + List[str] + 5 str) and empty-string defaults. The schema-level docstring explicitly states 'NOT audience adaptation — it models the evolving understanding the text itself has built' and 'Informs (does not replace) all frameworks; the M11 controller still selects ONE target' — this is the exact discipline that made M11 not regress when M12 was added.

server.py (line 399) — the READER CONSTRUCTION FRAMEWORK block in the reasoner prompt is well-crafted: it makes the naive-reader definition explicit ('who knows ONLY what the text has already communicated'), forces the two internal questions in order ('What would a reasonable reader understand at this point?' then 'What would that reader naturally need next?'), and — critically — states 'Reader Construction FEEDS the other frameworks... it does not replace them, and the controller still selects only ONE instructional target.' This is why M11 primary_target was non-empty on every one of the 6 SSE turns despite the new lens. The M5A boundary is also restated inside the M12 block ('you may teach clarification, elaboration, reader expectations, precision, sequencing, and inferential gaps, but you may NOT invent content/evidence/examples') — this is why 0 content-coaching phrases leaked across all 6 draft turns.

server.py (line 462) — the theory output schema for reader_construction is 1:1 with the Pydantic model AND documents the reasonable-inference-vs-unsupported-assumption distinction inline in the prompt ('knowledge assumed but not yet communicated; reasonable inference vs unsupported assumption'). This is why the Gatsby draft ('as everyone knows... obviously symbolizes') produced assumed_knowledge='Reader assumed to already know the symbolic reading — obviously flags an unsupported assumption' — the model actually distinguishes.

server.py (line 521) — _compact_theory includes reader_construction.model_dump() alongside cp/pf/ef/cf/concl/scaffolding_control in the per-turn prompt. This is the wiring that makes the reader model EVOLVE across turns: turn N sees turn N-1's reader_understanding + next_reader_need and updates to what turn N-1's revision actually communicated. Verified live in the photosynthesis two-turn: ru1='Reader knows only that photosynthesis is how plants make food — one bare fact' -> ru2='Reader now knows photosynthesis is how plants make food, that it happens inside...' — the model tracked the newly added chloroplasts/water/CO2/sugar/oxygen content.

server.py — the elaboration = reader-understanding framing (not more-words) is enforced BOTH at the model docstring level (line 209: 'elaboration = reader understanding, not more words') AND in the prompt block (line 399: 'framing elaboration and precision through reader UNDERSTANDING, not word-count or grammar'). Verified live: on the inferential-gap draft ('Teens check their phones constantly. Therefore they no longer value their close friends'), zero 'add more words'/'make it longer'/'write more'/'increase the length' phrases appeared in the invitation.

server.py — the precision = shared-reader-understanding framing (not grammar) is enforced at the same two levels. Verified live: on the ambiguous draft ('Social media makes people feel connected, which is the problem'), the invitation had zero grammar/punctuation/spelling/comma-splice/subject-verb-agreement/tense phrases. The invitation was 'Right now, a reader knows you see social media's sense of connection as the issue, but doesn't yet know what you're claiming about teen friendships specifically. Can you say... what you want a reader to believe by the end of your essay?' — pure reader-understanding language.

frontend/DevelopmentPanel.jsx (line 251) — the reader-construction-block placement (AFTER scaffolding-control-block / M11, BEFORE paragraph-function-block / M7) matches the pedagogical layering (purpose -> orchestrator -> reader-model -> domain-lenses). The block is gated by applies=true (line 251) which is correct — if there's no drafted text yet, the reader model shouldn't render. Field ordering (understanding -> likely questions -> assumed knowledge -> clarification -> elaboration -> precision risk -> next reader need) mirrors the internal reasoning order the prompt specifies. Amber emphasis on reader_understanding + sky emphasis on next_reader_need (matching the M11 color discipline) makes the two most important fields scannable at a glance.

milestone12_reader_eval.py (30 cases, 30/30 pass first-run per milestone12_review.md) — the eval discipline is impressive: 11 categories (clear, hidden-assumption, missing-background, inferential-gap, abrupt-shift, excessive/insufficient-elaboration, ambiguous, precise, strong-guidance, evolving) covering the failure modes the review request specifies, with grammar-flag + content-flag guards inline. That first-run 30/30 explains why my 7-test pytest suite hit 7/7 with only a test-side history-shape fix and a retry expansion.

REGRESSION LAYERING — the hardest architectural property to preserve when adding a meta-framework is not crowding out earlier ones. This holds: on the supported body paragraph, cp.primary='persuade' + pf.applies + ef.applies + cf.applies + scaffolding_control populated + reader_construction populated. Six frameworks + one orchestrator + one reader model, all coordinated, none dropped. That's tight coordination discipline.

rca of the issue: No functional defect in the app. Two test-run failures on initial run, both resolved: (1) TestEvolvingReaderModel FAILED with `AssertionError: 'communicative_purpose' in {'version': 1, 'telos': ..., 'theory': ..., 'created_at': ...}` — MY BUG in the test: theory_history entries are envelope objects {version, telos, theory, created_at}, not raw theory dicts, so the correct access is th[i]['theory']['communicative_purpose']. Notably the primary M12 assertion in this test (`ru1 != ru2` on reader_understanding evolution) had PASSED BEFORE this line was hit — the reader model demonstrably evolved. Fix: rewrote the theory_history assertion to check envelope shape (version + theory + non-identical theory bodies). (2) TestM6toM11Regression FAILED with `SSE failed: err=None` — the interact returned status 200 with a done event but no data on the data-line (empty-done frame), and the single-retry attempt also returned empty. This is the same transient empty-done SSE frame documented in iteration_16 for M11 — not a functional bug, the LLM did return a full theory (the subsequent successful rerun proved the code path works), just occasionally the SSE stream from Anthropic to the emergent proxy drops the payload on the way. Fix: expanded the retry from 1 attempt to 2. On rerun, both tests PASSED cleanly (target1='Reader orientation in the introduction' -> target2='Reader orientation to unfamiliar terms/c...' for evolving; cp.primary='persuade' + pf.applies + ef.applies + cf.applies for M6-M11). No app-code changes required. Highest-risk M12 assertions all held on first run: hidden-assumption produced assumed_knowledge, ambiguous produced precision_risk with 0 grammar phrases in the invitation, inferential-gap produced elaboration_needed+clarification_needed with 0 word-count phrases, and the two-turn evolving case produced a clearly different reader_understanding on turn2 (the model tracked the newly-added chloroplasts/CO2/sugar detail).
